M01.reason: Edge-16 end-of-transfer handling would run at the wrong edge count, so the transfer length, join, Trail and Pause entry would break.

M02.reason: With OR, o_mosi would shift on every SCLK edge, not only on the shift edges, so MOSI bit timing would be wrong.

M03.reason: The shift edge would move to the sampling edge, so MOSI would change at the sampling edge instead of a half period away.

M04.reason: Trail would end on the wrong cycles, so o_cs_n would not rise exactly D cycles after SCLK edge 16.

M05.reason: o_rsp_valid would not be raised at the end of a transfer, so the received byte is never shown.

M06.reason: r_last is always overwritten at the accepting handshake in Idle before any use. It only affects cmd_ready in XFER and the XFER end, and cmd_ready in Idle does not depend on it. The reset value is not observable at the ports.

M07.reason: With AND, a new byte would be loaded into the shown register only when it is not valid and the consumer is ready, so the byte would go to held or be mishandled.

M08.reason: SCLK edges would be generated outside the transfer state and none inside it, so o_sclk would never toggle in a transfer.

M09.reason: xfer_last_cycle would be true at every SCLK edge, so responses would load and cmd_ready would assert early.

M10.reason: MOSI would shift only at the final edge and not at the normal shift edges, so the data and the hold of d[0] would break.

M11.reason: The response would be captured at every cycle except the last cycle of a transfer, so the received byte is lost or wrong.

M12.reason: A byte received under back-pressure would not be marked held, so it would be lost.

M13.reason: o_rsp_valid would be 1 in reset instead of 0.

M14.reason: The half-period tick would fire on every count but the last, so SCLK timing would be wrong.

M15.reason: cmd_ready in XFER would be 1 whenever the last cycle comes or the shown byte is absent, so commands would be accepted in mid-transfer.

M16.reason: The response block would be in reset while i_rst_n=1 and run while in reset, so no response would be produced and reset would not clear the outputs.

M17.reason: The Idle gap counter would never advance, so cmd_ready would stay blocked after o_cs_n rises for D>1.

M18.reason: The case covers all four r_state values and every branch overwrites cmd_ready, so the default assignment is never visible.

M19.reason: The CPHA used to launch the first MOSI bit would be inverted in its source, so the first MOSI bit would be wrong when the mode changes just before a burst start or at a join.

M20.reason: A response handshake would be seen when only one side is ready, so bytes would be dropped or o_rsp_valid cleared wrongly.

M21.reason: The end-of-transfer branch would be taken at the wrong edge count, so the transfer length and phases would break.

M22.reason: The Trail counter would not advance, so Trail would never end for D>1 and o_cs_n would not rise.

M23.reason: The held flag would stay set after the held byte is promoted, so the byte would be duplicated and o_rsp_valid would not fall.

M24.reason: xfer_last_cycle would fire at every SCLK edge except edge 16, so the transfer end and response load would break.

M25.reason: i_miso would be sampled at every SCLK edge, so the received byte would be wrong.

M26.reason: The MOSI data would be loaded when no handshake occurs and not at the handshake, so the transmitted byte would be wrong.

M27.reason: o_cs_n would be 0 in reset instead of 1.

M28.reason: A held byte would be set by reset and later appear as a spurious response.

M29.reason: i_miso would be sampled on the wrong SCLK edges (the other phase), so the received byte would be wrong.

M30.reason: cmd_ready in XFER would also be 1 whenever o_rsp_valid=0, so commands would be accepted in mid-transfer.

M31.reason: The shown byte would be consumed or promoted when no response handshake occurs, and it would not be released at a handshake.

M32.reason: The half-period counter would not advance during a transfer, so SCLK would stall for D>1.

M33.reason: r_sclk reset value 1 or 0 is hidden while o_cs_n=1, because o_sclk = i_cpol in that case. r_sclk is loaded with i_cpol at the burst-start handshake before o_cs_n falls, so the reset value never reaches o_sclk.

M34.reason: A command would be accepted when only i_cmd_valid or only o_cmd_ready is 1.

M35.reason: The rx shift register would be held at reset while i_rst_n=1 and would shift while in reset, so the received data would be wrong.

M36.reason: o_cs_n would stay low after Trail and not be released at the end of a burst.
